claim: Collaborators can attach attributed positive and negative examples to shared heuristics; disconnected additions and exact-parent removals retain history and converge without exposing research bodies through MCP inspection.
verified: Positive and negative example events use a versioned peer-namespaced immutable ledger inside the existing discussions map
Exact duplicate delivery is idempotent while reused event identity and disconnected public-root collisions fail closed
Concurrent positive and negative additions survive duplicate and reversed Yjs delivery and converge deterministically
Concurrent exact-parent removals survive merge, retain attributed history, and converge
Missing heuristics, malformed records, control bytes, and oversized bodies are rejected without shared mutation
The engine-free product surface creates/selects heuristics and adds or explicitly removes attributed examples
Loading and mutation failures are exposed through accessible status and alert states
Research-state inspection returns only bounded counts and integrity metadata, omitting example bodies and display-name attribution
All new visual treatments use existing theme tokens
Production TypeScript and Vite build passes
limitations: No packaged two-install interaction or physical Drive/LAN example edit is included in this proof.
Researcher identity is installation-provided and is not authenticated.
Examples are collaborative research inputs; this capability does not score them, prove truth, or run an evaluation engine.
Removal retains immutable history; the product does not yet expose that removed-history audit trail.
